figures.alt: Photo of a lighthouse on a Lake Michigan breakwater at dusk with a bright beam of light sweeping over the water.
figures.caption: A lighthouse shines a light in a pattern that sailors far away can see.

figures.alt: Photo of a yellow rubber duck riding gentle waves on a lake.
figures.caption: A wave moves forward, but the duck mostly moves up and down.

figures.alt: Interactive: sliders change the amplitude and wavelength of a moving rope wave, with a cork that moves up and down while the wave moves forward.
figures.caption: Change a rope wave’s height and length and watch the cork bob.

figures.alt: Interactive: a lamp, apple and eye, with the lamp on or off, and a toggle that shows the wrong idea of eye beams crossed out.
figures.caption: See how light gets to your eye, and why light does not shoot out of your eyes.

figures.alt: Bar graph, How far a wave moved an object. Small wave 1 cm (about 1/2 inch), Large wave 3 cm (about 1 1/4 inches).
figures.caption: A small wave moved the floating object 1 cm (about 1/2 inch). A large wave moved it 3 cm (about 1 1/4 inches). Bigger waves carry more energy.
